verdict: PASS - benign stream not trivially separable
caveat: n=20 is the sprint-plan sample size, not a powered experiment: the 95% CI spans roughly +/-20 points, so this check reliably catches TRIVIAL separability (the >90% case it is designed for) and cannot resolve, say, 55% from 70%. Report it as the screen it is.

labeller.inputs_read: analysis/blind_check_unlabelled.md only; no key, no streams, no sampler, no templates
labeller.caveat: The pre-registered design says 'B labels them'. These labels are an LLM's, disclosed by B unprompted. An LLM is arguably a STRONGER adversary than a human skimming (systematic, tireless) and arguably weaker (no ops intuition). Report the labeller explicitly in the paper; do not present this as a human blind check.

stratified_by_B_self_report.note: B declared in advance which windows were decided by a real signal vs a guess. Scored after the fact.
stratified_by_B_self_report.finding: All accuracy is carried by the windows B flagged as having a real tell (7/7, p=0.008). The other 13 are at chance (7/13, p=0.500). The 70% headline is one template pair, not broad separability.

template_audit.method: diffed every PHASE_TEMPLATES entry's event against its benign_twin
template_audit.row_exposure: ~5.8% of rows in each stream carry a perfectly-separating literal
template_audit.window_exposure: ~50% of 5-minute windows contain at least one such literal
template_audit.lexical_ceiling: A labeller using ONLY these literals scores 100% on the ~50% of windows it can decide and must guess on the rest -> expected ~75% overall. That is the ceiling for a perfect per-line lexical adversary, and it is BELOW the 90% threshold. On this sample that rule got 14/14 decided correct, 6 undecidable.
template_audit.interpretation: The control survives an optimal lexical attack, which is the claim that matters. But the tells are perfect where present, so surface separability is ~75%, not ~50%. Report that number rather than implying the streams are indistinguishable.
template_audit.recommendation: Most differing twins encode REAL behavioural differences (attacker breadth, third-party drop hosts, shred vs rm) and templates.py RULE 3 keeps them deliberately - removing them would model the problem away. The exception is cmd.json vs job.json, which is a pure naming artifact with no behavioural content and is a free tell across dropper+c2. Neutralising just that one is the cheap win. Not changed here: it would require regenerating both streams and would move every downstream number (escalation #10498, E0 baselines).
